status_summary: On 2026-06-23 HHS's Office of Population Affairs posted a 63.4 million dollar funding opportunity to replicate effective Teen Pregnancy Prevention programs, requiring sexual risk avoidance education, promotion of delayed sexual initiation, advance parent notice and opt-out, and program eligibility under stated criteria, and on 2026-06-26 HHS terminated 53 of 67 grants, about 68 million dollars, citing misalignment with agency priorities. On 2026-08-19 the federal district court in Washington, DC preliminarily enjoined HHS from implementing its 2026 Teen Pregnancy Prevention policy, including the FY2026 funding notices, finding the policy likely arbitrary and capricious, while declining to reinstate the terminated grants. A joint status report of 2026-09-01 reported no program updates from HHS and no appeal, and no awards under the 2026 notices were found. The stage is blocked because the instrument that redirected the program is enjoined, while the terminations remain in place.

uncertainties: The order does not state whether the injunction is limited to the plaintiffs; the memorandum opinion's operative portion was not fully visible, though the joint status report describes the injunction as barring implementation of the FY2026 notices. The terminations rest on news reports; the termination letters were not read. Whether HHS reissued notices, made any awards or let FY2026 funds lapse after 2026-09-01 was not found: the OPA award announcements page lists nothing after January 2025, and the replication opportunity on simpler.grants.gov shows as archived on 2026-09-01. No appeal was found in the sources read. PREP and funding parity were not examined.
